newsitem.title: CANADA: Molson says not considering special payout.
newsitem.headline: Molson says not considering special payout.

text.p: Canadian brewing and entertainment firm Molson Cos Ltd said on Wednesday that it was not considering a special dividend or share buyback despite pressure from some institutional shareholders.
"The board is not considering a special dividend at this time nor is it considering a share buyback," Norman Seagram, president and chief executive, told the company's annual meeting in Montreal.
Seagram said some institutional investors had pressured the company for a special distribution after the almost C$1 billion sale of non-core assets.
Seagram, who took over Molson's top job today, said the company would complete a full-scale study of international brewing opportunities in three months.
"We are looking strongly at Latin American and Chinese markets. Any sizeable investment we would make would be with partners or as a joint venture," Seagram said.

Some analysts have said Molson may buy a larger stake in its 40 percent-owned Molson Breweries. But Seagram suggested that was unlikely. Molson Breweries is also 40 percent-owned by Australia's Foster's Brewing Group Ltd and 20 percent by Philip Morris Cos Inc's Miller Brewing unit.
"Foster's has indicated no wish to change its 40 percent partnership in Molson Breweries and we continue to work with both Foster's and Miller," Seagram said.
Molson's outlook for the rest of the year is bright due to improving contributions from brewing and retailing, he said.

"In the first two months of the second quarter, Molson Breweries share of the domestic market improved from the first-quarter level," Seagram said, but he did not elaborate. Earlier this summer, Labatt Brewing Co Ltd, a unit of Belgian beer giant Interbrew SA, pulled ahead of its arch- rival in Canadian market share.
Seagram said Molson planned a careful and controlled divestment of its retail business holdings in due time, "but performance is improving strongly this year in line with the first quarter."

Molson Cos' net earnings for the first quarter ended June 30 rose to C$20.8 million from year earlier C$19.9 million. Sales edged up to C$399.7 million from C$397 million in the year ago first quarter.
Molson class B shares were up 0.25 at 21 in light volume today on the Toronto Stock Exchange. Molson class A stock was unchanged at 20.50.
